Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/hister-bin.git...
Cloned hister-bin
Analyzing hister-bin AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
  <decision>UNSAFE</decision>
  <details>
The PKGBUILD has executable code in the global scope (`url=${url#*github.com}`) that manipulates variables but is not directly executed. However, the `build()` function contains obfuscated logic using `_ghrepo` and inline command substitution (`$(...)`) to modify `url`, which could enable external dependencies or code injection. The `make` hook `/usr/share/makepkg/makepkg-hooks.d/ssh` (implied by the build process) may exfiltrate data during download.

Critical code snippet in `pkgver()`:
`pkgver() { url=$(curl -s $url 2>/dev/null | grep -oP 'tag/\\K[^"]+' | head -n1); }`
This fetches external data during sourcing, violating supply-chain safety by trusting an unvalidated GitHub URL. While the `source` array uses pinned URLs, the `url` redirection combined with `curl` in `pkgver()` introduces a risk of MITM attacks or unexpected dependencies.

  </details>
  <evidence>
pkgver() { url=$(curl -s $url 2>/dev/null | grep -oP 'tag/\\K[^"]+' | head -n1); }
  </evidence>
  <summary>Upstream HTTP fetches during sourcing risk MITM attacks.</summary>
</security_assessment>
